episodes.192177: The monsoon high over northern Arizona on July 19th continued backing west to over the Great Basin July 20th and 21st in response to upper level troughing over the central U.S. The upper level trough over the central U.S. helped bring a backdoor front through eastern NM early on July 20th. In between the two synoptic features, upper level disturbances travelled south through New Mexico. This resulted in a greater coverage of afternoon and evening showers and storms over the region both days with activity slowly waning overnight. Storms over the South Fork burn scar brought another round of flash flooding to the Ruidoso area Saturday afternoon with the Rio Ruidoso rising to a record level of 15.39 feet July 20th. Flash flooding was reported from storms in Portales mid Sunday afternoon. Another round of flash flooding occurred in Ruidoso Sunday night from storms moving south through the area. Daytime heating on Monday resulted in another crop of showers and storms mainly across the higher terrain Monday afternoon and evening moving south with time. Storms produced some flash flooding on the northeast part of the Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar and a peak wind gust of 62 mph on the White Sands Missile Range near Oscuro.
episodes.192196: Southeast flow around a high pressure center over southern Nevada brought some upper level tropical moisture to central California. With instability increasing over the Sierra Nevada during the afternoon scattered thunderstorms broke out, and some of them produced locally heavy rainfall.
episodes.192210: Scattered storms (a few supercells) produced strong and gusty winds over north Alabama during the late morning hours ahead of/along a trough axis ahead of a frontal boundary north of the area. Isolated tree damage was reported in the Tuscumbia area with a small weakly bowing line of storms.
episodes.192219: Heavy showers and thunderstorms ahead of a cold front led to flash flooding for portions of Washington County in Maryland.
episodes.192313: Scattered thunderstorms moved across northern Illinois during the afternoon and early evening of July 23rd producing isolated wind damage and isolated flooding.
episodes.192402: Slow moving thunderstorms produced minor flooding.
episodes.192406: A very marginal pulse severe thunderstorm produced a 60 mph wind gust.
episodes.192443: A couple of thunderstorms produced localized wind gusts over the tidal Potomac River and middle Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.192581: A severe thunderstorm in Ajo resulted in a wind gust of 59 mph.
episodes.192668: Strong storms during the early morning hours in western Minnesota generated hail to the size of quarters and winds approaching 60 mph. The combination of hail and high winds resulted in damage to the siding and roof of at least one home, and shredded nearby crops 6 miles east of Wheaton.
episodes.192693: A stalled frontal boundary across the Mid Atlantic helped to spark an isolated severe thunderstorm. Winds from this thunderstorm snapped up to thirty trees in Stokes County.
episodes.192694: A stalled frontal boundary across the Mid Atlantic helped to spark an isolated severe thunderstorm. Winds from this thunderstorm blew down two trees in Halifax County. The storm also produced a funnel cloud.
episodes.193475: Classic summertime pattern favored the development of strong storms, with one such storm becoming severe. This caused a downburst and resulted in wind damage in Richland County. Strong moisture convergence and high precipitable water several hours later caused training thunderstorms over downtown Columbia leading to flash flooding.
episodes.193730: Slow moving thunderstorms produced very heavy rain and some flash flooding in the Greenville area.
episodes.194130: An upper-level trough moved across a stationary front and a very moist airmass. This combination generated thunderstorms. Some of these storms produced heavy rainfall that led to flash flooding.
episodes.194206: A few severe thunderstorms developed along the M-59 corridor, producing both hail and damaging winds, with flooding also occuring over parts of Macomb and Wayne counties. Rainfall totals of 2 to 2.5 inches were observed over a short period.
episodes.194207: Thunderstorms moving through Lake St. Clair produced winds up to 50 knots.
episodes.194296: A shortwave trough, crossing an environment with up to 2000 J/kg of surface-based CAPE and marginal shear, created a broken line of thunderstorms across eastern Ohio during the afternoon of July 23rd.  The strongest of these storms created several instances of wind damage in Coshocton County.
episodes.194307: A thunderstorm produced a 61 mph wind gust at the Sharpnose RAWS site near Hudson.
episodes.194328: An upper trough draped across the central and eastern U.S. and a stalled front over Central Texas combined to generated scattered showers and thunderstorms July 21 through July 23. Most of the storms remained sub-severe, but a few generated heavy rain and flash flooding in some locations, and one storm produced a damaging microburst in Hood County on the 21st.
episodes.194468: North to northwest flow aloft continued with another upper trough moving through New Mexico.  Severe thunderstorms developed over the Tularosa Basin and produced a couple of wind gusts of 58 mph to 66 mph.
episodes.194485: Conditions were favorable for waterspout development in the morning hours along the southeast South Carolina coast. Lines of showers developed just offshore along the land breeze, with plentiful low-level moisture and light surface winds.
episodes.194511: A shortwave trough brought a cold front through southeast Oregon. This cold front brought a significant shift in the dry and hot weather with high based thunderstorms and associated winds. Strong winds, especially in Baker County, brought minor damage to several small cities.
episodes.194528: In an environment characterized by PWAT values of around 1.5 with MLCAPE values near 1000 J/KG, thunderstorm activity developed across the Mohave Desert during the early afternoon hours. An isolated strong thunderstorm developed over the higher terrain area of Joshua Tree National Park, where it remained anchored and dumped over an inch of rain in less than one hour, enough rainfall in a short time span to cause road closures due to flooding.
episodes.194633: Slow moving thunderstorms in combination with abundant tropical moisture produced heavy rainfall resulting in flash flooding in portions of Kimble County.
episodes.194687: Thunderstorms developed over the Devils Lake Basin along a southerly moving surface boundary. Eventually the storms moved into the northern James River Valley, producing estimated 60 mph wind gusts near Carrington, in Foster County, along with nickel size hail.
episodes.194763: Afternoon and evening thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze produce strong marine wind gusts over the Nature Coast, and central to southwest areas near Clearwater and Venice.
episodes.194764: Afternoon thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze produce a brief land spout tornado near Lake Wales in Polk County after moving inland.
episodes.194778: Main hazards were hail and wind in Northeastern North Dakota and Northwestern Minnesota.
episodes.194779: Main hazards were hail and wind in Northeastern North Dakota and Northwestern Minnesota.
episodes.194812: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a stationary front in the Atlanta metro and towards Macon. Heavy rainfall was the main threat, however isolated wind damage and strong storms were able to develop through the afternoon along a line stretching from between Atlanta and Macon up through Athens.
episodes.194823: High pressure to the west continued to advect much drier air across northern and central portions of eastern Utah and western Colorado resulting in a downturn in storm coverage. However, a small pocket of deep subtropical moisture still remained over the eastern San Juans and Archuleta County, resulting in a few stronger storms that produced heavy rainfall rates and localized flash flooding. One particular storm resulted in a debris flow over Archuleta County near Chimney Rock.
episodes.194834: Low pressure aloft over the Great Lakes featured a southward moving surface cold front located across central MN and western WI. A line of thunderstorms developed during the evening of July 22nd and produced strong winds.
episodes.194840: Slow moving thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon and early evening hours and produced heavy rainfall across eastern Scott County.  This lead to flash flooding that damage roads near LeClaire Iowa.
episodes.194974: Monsoon moisture advecting around the periphery of the big ridge causing excessive heat fueled scattered thunderstorms. Several storms produced high winds and/or flooding.
episodes.194976: Monsoon moisture trapped under the big ridge causing excessive heat fueled isolated thunderstorms. A few storms produced high winds and/or flooding.
episodes.195017: A stationary front was draped just northwest of the area, while southwesterly flow aloft was adding moisture to the vertical column. Early evening convection produced localized flash flooding.
episodes.195149: A moist and unstable air mass was in place with dew points generally in the mid to upper 70s on July 23, 2024. This resulted in scattered heavy rain and flooding across portions of Central Virginia.
episodes.195993: At the surface, a cold front drifted southeastward from the Upper MS River Valley to far-southwestern ON, far-western Lake Erie, and northwest OH between the early afternoon of the 23rd and late morning of the 24th as a low moved east-northeastward from central Lake Michigan to Georgian Bay. The cold front then advanced farther southeastward to eastern Lake Erie, northwest PA, and northeast OH by the early evening of the 24th as the low moved northeastward to southwestern QC. This cold front encountered a warm and humid sector along the northwestern flank of the Bermuda-Azores subtropical high pressure ridge. Along and ahead of the cold front, several rounds of multicell thunderstorms impacted northeast OH and generated damaging straight-line convective wind gusts. These storms occurred in an environment comprised of moderate effective bulk shear, MUCAPE, and DCAPE, respectively.
